exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Ether (ETH) traded at $2,342.50 as of 2026-10-25 16:47:57 UTC, +0.13% over one hour and +1.68% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $2,313.32 to $2,368.07; spot sits at 53% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is -1.38% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($2,342.07) is below the 72-hour average ($2,370.76). Spot is 6.80% below the seven-day high of $2,513.51 and 1.65% above the seven-day low of $2,304.39.

exhibits.title: Volatility & Momentum
exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 2.31% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 40.2, conventionally neutral.

exhibits.title: Liquidity
exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $6.28 billion, equal to 2.20% of the $286.05 billion market capitalization.

exhibits.title: Market Sentiment
exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 54 ("Neutral"), versus 53 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink ETH/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $2,339.84, 47 minutes before the spot quote and -0.11% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price is firmly above the 24‑hour low ($2,313.32) and sits at 53% of the daily range, indicating that upward pressure remains intact and a breakout above the midpoint ($2,340.70) is statistically more probable than a reversal toward the low [Ex. B].  

2. Realized volatility is modest at 2.31% per day, while the RSI of 40.2 signals a market that is not yet oversold, providing a stable backdrop for a long bias without the risk of abrupt pull‑backs [Ex. D].  

3. Liquidity is robust, with $6.28 billion traded in the last 24 hours—2.20% of market cap—ensuring that a paper long position can be entered and exited cleanly, while the neutral Fear & Greed Index (54) reflects an environment conducive to steady price appreciation rather than panic selling [Ex. E, F].  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price is firmly entrenched in the upper half of its 24‑hour range (53% of range) and has risen 0.13% in the last hour, indicating immediate buying pressure that is likely to sustain a modest upside over the next 24 hours [Ex. A, B].  

2. Despite a seven‑day downtrend, volatility remains low at 2.31% per day and the RSI is neutral at 40.2, suggesting the market is not primed for a sharp reversal and will likely trade sideways or slightly higher rather than plunge [Ex. C, D].  

3. Liquidity is robust with $6.28 billion traded in 24 hours, and sentiment is neutral (Fear & Greed Index 54), providing a stable backdrop that supports a short‑term bullish bias without exposing the Bear to outsized risk [Ex. E, F].  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s first point collapses under Exhibit B: the price sits at only 53 % of the 24‑hour range, essentially the midpoint, not the “upper half,” and the range’s upper bound is merely $2,368.07, a trivial 1.1 % premium to spot—insufficient to infer sustained buying pressure.  

The second point ignores Exhibit C: the seven‑day average is declining, with the 24‑hour average $2,342.07 below the 72‑hour average $2,370.76, indicating a down‑trend that outweighs any neutral RSI reading. The market’s inertia favours further weakness, not a bullish bias.  

Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s first point collapses on the range statistics. Although the spot sits at 53% of the 24‑hour range, Exhibit B shows the price is 6.80% below the seven‑day high, indicating a dominant downtrend that outweighs any short‑term midpoint bias. The second point relies on a “neutral” RSI, yet Exhibit D’s realized volatility of 2.31% per day, coupled with the 1.38% seven‑day decline in Exhibit C, signals weakening momentum, not stability. Thus the market lacks bullish impetus and a short‑term correction is more plausible. Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds the evidence insufficient to justify a practice position.

findings.finding: Spot price up 0.13% hour and 1.68% day shows modest short‑term strength
Seven‑day price trend is down 1.38% and price sits 6.80% below the seven‑day high
Realized volatility low at 2.31% and RSI 40.2 neutral indicate limited momentum
Fear & Greed Index at 54 (Neutral) reflects no strong sentiment bias

ruling.opinion: The record shows modest intraday gains (Ex. A) but a broader seven‑day decline (Ex. C) and price near the lower half of its recent range. Low volatility and a neutral RSI (Ex. D) suggest limited directional force, while sentiment remains neutral (Ex. F). No exhibit convincingly predicts a sustained move either way, so the Court cannot endorse a long or short practice position.
ruling.dissent: Given the recent price uptick and neutral sentiment, a modest long position could be justified despite the seven‑day downtrend.

sentence.reason: The case was dismissed; no practice position is ordered.
